Paleomagnetic constraint on the formation of the Eastern Himalayan
Syntaxis: A new late Eocene result from the Mangkang area of the
eastern Tibetan Plateau
Zijian Zhanga, Yabo Tongb,c,∗ , Shuchen Jina, Xinxin Suna, Lifu Houb,c, Junling Peib,c,
Zhenyu
Yanga,∗∗
aCollege of Resources, Environment and Tourism, Capital Normal University, Beijing 100048, China
bKey Laboratory of Paleomagnetism and Tectonic Reconstruction of the Ministry of Natural Resource, Beijing 100081, China
cInstitute of Geomechanics, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, Beijing 100081, China
a r t i c l e i n f o a b s t r a c t
Article history: The Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis (EHS) is a major structural and geomorphological unit in Eastern
Received 20 September 2022 Tibet; however, its mechanism of formation and the extent of its northward effect of compression
Received in revised form 8 December 2022 remain unclear. To address these questions, we conducted a paleomagnetic and geochronologic study

Keywords: Mangkang area was located at a paleolatitude of 20.5 ± 0.9 ◦ N during the late Eocene. A comparison
Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis of paleolatitudes of the Qiangtang block with those inferred from the apparent polar wander paths
Paleomagnetism (APWP) of India and Eurasia suggests that the Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis was formed after 35 Ma
late Eocene when Eurasia was penetrated by ∼600 km by northward-moving India. This is consistent with geologic
southeastern Tibetan Plateau evidence of intra-continental shortening in the foreland of the Eastern Himalayan syntaxis. The northward
counterclockwise penetration of the corner of India also resulted in the large right-lateral strike-slip
system of the Sagaing fault (SGF), with ∼400-600 km of displacement between the EHS and the Shan-
Thai block. Thus, the northward wedging of the EHS indicates minimal southward displacement of
the Shan-Thai block. Our results link the tectonic activity of the EHS to the lateral extrusion of the
southeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, providing a new perspective on the evolution of this region
since the late Eocene.
